title: Plaintiff's Response to Defendant [NAME] First Set of Discovery Requests

body.text: NOW COMES Plaintiff [NAME], pro se, and for his Answer to Defendant [NAME] (“[SHORT]”) First set of Discovery Requests to Plaintiff [NAME] as follows:

ANSWER: [Answer fully under oath, or state the specific objection and its reason under Wis. Stat. § 804.08(1)(b). Identify any part answered and any part withheld. A timely, specific objection may be served in place of the objected-to answer; do not confuse it with a total failure to serve answers or objections under § 804.12(4). Request protective relief under § 804.01(3) when needed. Include only facts and objections supported by the actual request and investigation.]

ANSWER: [State that inspection and related activities will be permitted as requested, or state the specific objection and reasons under Wis. Stat. § 804.09(2)(b)1. If objecting only in part, specify that part and permit inspection of the remainder. Identify actual responsive non-privileged materials and the production arrangements, or describe the reasonable search supporting a truthful no-documents response. Supplement as required by § 804.01(5).]

ANSWER: [Admit; specifically deny; truthfully qualify or admit part and deny the remainder; or state a proper objection and reasons. Lack of information or knowledge requires reasonable inquiry and a statement that the information known or readily obtainable is insufficient to admit or deny. See Wis. Stat. § 804.11(1)(b).]

I, [NAME], am the [Plaintiff/Defendant] in this action. I have read the foregoing Answers to [PARTY]'s [First] Set of Interrogatories. Pursuant to Wis. Stat. § 887.015, I declare under penalty of false swearing under the law of Wisconsin that the foregoing answers are true and correct to the best of my knowledge, information, and belief.
Signed on the ____ day of __________, [YEAR], at [CITY], [STATE].

[Wis. Stat. § 804.08(1)(b): the person making the interrogatory answers signs their verification; an attorney making objections signs those objections when the party is represented. A self-represented answering party signs in their own capacity and does not need a fictitious second attorney signer. Use the actual person qualified to answer, including the appropriate officer or agent for an entity. Remove this drafting note before service.]
